chunks: And through this chain of narration, from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad (all of them), from Ribi'i, from Fudayl, who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Increase in the recitation of Tahleel (La ilaha illallah) and Takbeer (Allahu Akbar), for there is nothing more beloved to Allah than Takbeer and Tahleel.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِير: Recitation of 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest)
key_terms.التَّهْلِيل: Recitation of 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act of remembrance to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the supreme merit of *Tahleel* (declaring God's oneness) and *Takbeer* (declaring God's greatness) as the most beloved acts of remembrance to Allah. In Shia scholarly tradition, this emphasis underscores the foundational role of monotheistic affirmation in purifying the soul and securing divine favor, linking verbal dhikr directly to spiritual proximity.
